newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end the day down, Jardine surges.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end the day down, Jardine surges.

text.p: Singapore shares slipped again on Friday closing the trading week on the same downward trend from which it started with no sign of an upturn in the immediate future, dealers said.
"It's been a difficult week and looks like there's another one to follow," said one dealer with a local brokerage.
The Straits Times Industrials Index ended down 11.41 at 2,032.30 with most of the drag exerted on the index by Fraser & Neave which fell 60 cents to Singapore $10.50.
Most interest though centred on Hong Kong-based Jardine Group stocks listed on the Singapore bourse.

HongKong Land Holdings saw a massive 27.4 million shares traded, more than 15 percent of the market's 166 million total, ending the day up US$0.22 at US$2.95, while Jardine Matheson leapt US$0.95 to a year-high of US$8.30.

The rise was sparked by speculation that the group would seek to relist its shares in Hong Kong after the territory is handed back to China at the end of June and on market talk of a call warrant placement deal.
